author: ValWood
body:
* **InterPro ID / label**

InterPro:IPR001962 
Molecular Function | asparagine synthase (glutamine-hydrolyzing) activity
Biological Process | asparagine biosynthetic process

UniProtKB-KW:KW-0061 human/pombe
Biological Process | asparagine biosynthetic process

* **Example sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**

https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q9NWL6/entry InterPro:IPR001962 & UniProtKB-KW:KW-0061 

https://www.pombase.org/gene/SPBC4F6.11c  UniProtKB-KW:KW-0061 

* **Description of issue**


This protein is a conserved unknown. It's in the same family as asparagine synthase, but does not appear to have asparagine synthase activity.


it contains a domain that resembles asparagine synthetases, but  as it is  a universally conserved  orthologous group it's likely to be doing something slightly different, though related.
title: InterPro:IPR001962 UniProtKB-KW:KW-0061

author: blazaropinto
body:
Hi Val,

Thanks very much for that. I see these proteins are indeed not included in IPR006426 (Asparagine synthase, glutamine-hydrolyzing). I removed those terms from IPR001962. I can't really find the publication you mention though, to update the description properly, could you please share the PMID/link to it?

Thanks,
Beatriz

author: ValWood
body:
Sorry, the reference was nonsense. I thought I had checked them all but I missed this one.

But for various reasons I'm not sure that this is an Asparagine synthase, and for such a conserved family member this must have been tested. 

In fission yeast asn2 can't substitute for asn1 (because asn1 is used as an auxotrophic marker for asparagine) so it is unlikely to be asparagine biosynthesis.

author: blazaropinto
body: Ok no problem, as an example of a probable different activity I added another case `This domain is also found in Asparagine synthetase domain-containing protein 1 from Mus musculus (ASND1), which is associated with a progressive degenerative myopathy PMID:32638637.`
